rounds.text: Pasupati Acrylon Ltd is trading at a heavily discounted valuation of 6.51x P/E and an EV/EBITDA of 4.51x, representing a massive discount relative to sector benchmarks of 20.35x and 10.77x respectively [E1, E6, E11]. This low multiple is entirely disconnected from the company’s elite profitability, highlighted by an exceptional return on capital employed (ROCE) of 19.63% and return on equity (ROE) of 16.06%, both dramatically outperforming sector averages [E8, E9, E10]. Operational momentum is explosive, evidenced by a 271% surge in trailing twelve-month profit growth alongside operating margins expanding by 11 percentage points to 14% [E21, E30]. Furthermore, the business is conservatively financed with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25x and generated robust free cash flow of Rs 40 Crore in March 2026, supported by positive institutional money flow [E36, E37, E43]. Conceded: the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% and a low 3-year average return on equity of 11.1% [E4, E60]. Nevertheless, the rules-based screen scores the business at a high-confidence 97 out of 100, driven by immense acceleration in sales and net profit [E61, E62, E63].

Pasupati Acrylon Ltd carries significant capital-allocation risks for shareholders, highlighted most starkly by a complete zero percent dividend yield despite the company reporting repeated profits [E4, E59]. Furthermore, the company has a low return on equity of 11.1% over the last three years, showing that past capital hasn't worked efficiently for ordinary investors [E60]. Conceded: the company displays a low debt-toacylglycerol equity ratio of 0.25x and generated positive operating cash flow [E37, E35]. However, the new 150 KL per day grain-based ethanol plant suffered cost overruns due to civil work, pushing expenditures from an assessed Rs 167 crore to roughly Rs 188 crore [E80]. This reliance on capital expenditure overruns combines with high annualised volatility of 49.7% and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -58.9% [E53, E52]. Finally, the business faces structural vulnerability from global raw material, energy, and coal volatility, alongside import dependence that leaves profit margins exposed to USD versus INR foreign exchange fluctuations [E90, E92].

Conceded: [E4] and [E59] regarding the zero percent dividend yield and the board's decision not to recommend a dividend [E87]. However, the low 3-year average return on equity cited by the bear [E60] is vastly eclipsed by the company's current reality, featuring a TTM ROE of 17.6% [E13] and an ROA of 14.99% [E8] that drastically outperform sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Conceded: [E80] concerning the ethanol plant cost overrun from Rs 167 crore to Rs 188 crore; nevertheless, this project is already fully operational, generating strong operating cash flow of Rs 52 crore and free cash flow of Rs 40 crore while maintaining a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.25x [E35, E36, E37, E78]. While the bear highlights historical drawdowns and volatility [E52, E53], the stock is currently trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with positive institutional money flow [E43, E49]. Finally, the bear's warning regarding foreign exchange and raw material exposure [E90, E92] is offset by massive operational efficiency gains, including a TTM operating margin jump of +11 percentage points to 14% and a quarterly surge to 16% [E30, E31, E81].

While the bull highlights a recent ROE of 17.6% [E13], the median ROE over the last three and five years remains much lower at 11% and 12% respectively [E27, E28], reflecting a cyclical earnings profile that is seasonally weak in June and September [E57]. Conceded: The ethanol plant is now operational [E78] with low debt-to-equity [E37], but the bull overlooks that the project faced a cost overrun to Rs 188 crore [E80] and missed its original September 2024 commencement target [E95] by six months [E78]. Despite reported cash flows [E35, E36], cash conversion is only moderate at 0.74x [E34], and the board continues to refuse dividend payments [E59, E87] or transfers to general reserves [E89]. The bull's technical optimism ignores that the stock is price-led, with five-year price growth of 18% exceeding profit growth of 10% [E55], while investors face high annualized volatility of 49.7% [E53] and a record drawdown of -58.9% [E52]. Finally, recent margin gains [E30, E31] are precarious given the company's admitted dependence on imports [E92], an inconsistent quarterly margin trend [E33], and the impact of volatile crude, coal, and energy prices on global consumption [E90, E91].

Conceded: [E27, E28], historical median ROE figures are lower, but the recent figures stand at a superior 16.06% to 17.6% [E9, E13], driven by a structural shift in operating margins up to 14%–16% [E30, E31]. Conceded: [E80, E95], the ethanol plant faced cost overruns and a timeline delay, but it is successfully commissioned and commercially producing at a now-enhanced 180 KL per day capacity [E78, E79], instantly adding a high-growth revenue stream supported by national E20 blending tailwinds [E93]. While the bear points to a zero dividend [E4, E59], this cash is being powerfully retained within a conservatively financed balance sheet carrying a low debt-to-equity of 0.25x [E37], generating substantial free cash flow of Rs 40 crore [E36]. The bear’s concern over volatility and drawdowns [E52, E53] ignores pristine price momentum, evidenced by a relative-strength rating of 100 [E50], a 12-month return of 62.1% [E51], and a rules-based screen score of 97 out of 100 [E61]. Finally, the massive discount is undeniable: a P/E of 6.51x [E1] trading against a sector benchmark of 20.35x [E6], alongside an intrinsic DCF value leaving a 71.4% margin of safety [E44, E45].

Conceded: the company records recent ROE figures of 16.06% to 17.6% [E9, E13]. However, the bull's optimism glosses over a multi-year track record of low returns, specifically a low median return on equity of 11.1% over the last 3 years [E60] and a 5-year median ROE of just 12% [E27]. The bull dismisses the zero dividend yield [E4], but the filed statements explicitly flag as a negative that the company is not paying out a dividend despite reporting repeated profits [E59]. The bull's reliance on the newly commissioned ethanol plant ignores the operational missteps explicitly documented in the annual report, including project cost overruns from civil work that inflated the budget from Rs 167 crore to around Rs 188 crore [E80], alongside a delayed commercial timeline that missed the initial target of September 2024 before starting in March 2025 [E78, E95]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on price momentum and a relative-strength rating of 100 [E50] completely ignores the severe historical risk profile of the stock, which carries a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -58.9% [E52] and high annualised volatility of 49.7% [E53]. Finally, the bull treats the low P/E multiple of 6.51x [E1] as an unmitigated bargain, but this must be weighed against the company's cyclical earnings profile [E57] and vulnerability to volatile raw material, energy, and coal costs that impact global acrylic fibre consumption [E90], as well as foreign exchange exposure from import dependence [E92].
